microphone.heading: Microphone access
microphone.intro: This device is reached over plain HTTP at an internal IP address ({origin}). Chrome blocks microphone access on insecure origins, so the voice assistant won't work here unless you allow it manually. This isn't needed for sites served over HTTPS.
microphone.list_suffix: to the list, enable it, and relaunch Chrome.
microphone.chrome_intro: This device is reached over plain HTTP at an internal IP address ({origin}). Chrome blocks microphone access on insecure origins, so the voice assistant won't work here unless you allow it manually. This isn't needed for sites served over HTTPS.
microphone.chrome_list_suffix: to the list, set it to Enabled, and relaunch Chrome.
microphone.chromium_intro: This device is running Chromium ({origin}). Open-source Chromium lacks built-in Google Speech keys and requires enabling Cloud Speech-to-Text (OpenAI Whisper) in Settings, plus the insecure origin flag.
microphone.edge_intro: This device is reached over plain HTTP at an internal IP address ({origin}). Microsoft Edge blocks microphone access on insecure origins, so the voice assistant won't work here unless you allow it manually. This isn't needed for sites served over HTTPS.
microphone.edge_list_suffix: to the list, set it to Enabled, and relaunch Edge.
microphone.brave_intro: This device is reached over plain HTTP at an internal IP address ({origin}). Brave blocks microphone access on insecure origins, so the voice assistant won't work here unless you allow it manually. This isn't needed for sites served over HTTPS.
microphone.brave_list_suffix: to the list, set it to Enabled, and relaunch Brave.
microphone.firefox_intro: This device is running Mozilla Firefox. Firefox requires enabling Cloud Speech-to-Text (OpenAI Whisper) in Settings for voice assistant support.
microphone.safari_intro: This device is reached over plain HTTP at an internal IP address ({origin}). Safari strictly blocks microphone access on insecure origins and does not provide browser flags to bypass this restriction.
microphone.safari_https_req: To use the voice assistant in Safari, connect to Tilora over HTTPS (or localhost).
microphone.safari_cert_tip_title: Using a self-signed or private SSL certificate?
microphone.safari_ios_cert_tip: iOS / iPadOS: Install your root certificate profile, then go to Settings > General > About > Certificate Trust Settings and enable full trust for root certificates.
microphone.safari_mac_cert_tip: macOS: In Keychain Access, double-click your certificate, expand Trust, and select "Always Trust".
microphone.other_intro: This device is reached over plain HTTP at an internal IP address ({origin}). Most browsers block microphone access on insecure connections.
microphone.other_https_req: To use voice commands, connect to Tilora over a secure HTTPS connection or configure a reverse proxy with SSL.

detail.server_transcode_hint: The backend runs ffmpeg to transcode the raw stream to H.264 so it plays in-app. Works with any tuner model, but adds real CPU load per viewer on whatever device is running the backend.
detail.hwaccel_device_hint: Which GPU node the VAAPI/Quick Sync presets use. Usually /dev/dri/renderD128, but a machine with a second graphics device shifts it to renderD129 — run the diagnostics below to see what is actually there.
detail.ffmpeg_debug_hint: Raises ffmpeg's own log level so hardware setup and filter details show up in the backend log. Worth turning on while diagnosing a failure, noisy the rest of the time.
detail.thumbnails_enabled_hint: Generates a hover-preview thumbnail sprite the first time a completed recording is opened, cached to disk after that. Turn off on machines where that one-time ffmpeg pass is too costly.
detail.diagnostics_hint: Checks each step in turn — device passthrough, permissions, driver, and a real test encode through every preset. Takes a few seconds and does not need a free tuner.
detail.diagnostics_no_dri: /dev/dri is not present, so the backend cannot reach a GPU at all. In Docker, add the /dev/dri device passthrough to the backend service.
detail.diagnostics_process: Backend runs as uid {uid}, gid {gid}, groups {groups}.
detail.external_only_hint: No in-app player — channels only offer a raw stream link to open in an external player like VLC.
detail.xmltv_hint: "Now playing" titles are tried first from a HDHomeRun DVR subscription. If you don't have one, set an XMLTV guide URL here instead (the format used by Plex, Channels DVR, TVheadend, etc.) — its channel ids must match your HDHomeRun channel numbers (e.g. "4.1").
